clue.text: Host in new religion

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A host figure appears within some newly founded faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' tells you to rearrange HOST and IN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the traditional faith of Japan, centred on worship of kami spirits.

clue.text: Engineers judge a way to recover possession

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to deem is to judge or consider

explanation.surface: Army engineers assess the best method of getting property back.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) is a standard crossword abbreviation; 'a way to' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem is to buy back or reclaim something pawned or mortgaged.

clue.text: Lucky thing, to be so attractive!

definitions.text: Lucky thing, to be so attractive!

parts.words: Lucky thing, to be so attractive!
parts.note: a U-shaped charm traditionally brings good luck, and one made of iron that pulls metal is literally attractive

explanation.surface: Someone envies a fortunate, alluring person.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped magnet resembles the lucky charm hung over doors, and magnets attract.

clue.text: Formic say, this relief from indigestion

definitions.meaning: formic acid is the acid found in ants, so it is an example of an insect's acid
a remedy that neutralises stomach acid

explanation.surface: Something formic offers relief to a dyspeptic sufferer.
explanation.walkthrough: Formic acid takes its name from the Latin for ant, so split the answer into two words for the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an acid from ants, and a stomach remedy that neutralises excess acid.

clue.text: Display training of house plant?

parts.note: to air something is to display it, as with views or laundry
conditioning is training by repeated habit

explanation.surface: Showing off how one has trained a potted indoor plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house plant' is not a pot plant but machinery (plant) installed in a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling equipment in a building is plant, in the sense of installed machinery.

clue.text: Dismissed genuinely and cleanly

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
right can mean truly or correctly, as in rightly

explanation.surface: Someone was truly and fairly sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT is the cricket term for a dismissed batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely, at a stroke, without any qualification left over.

clue.text: US doctor, given a quarter, is one detained for the duration

parts.note: an interne (or intern) is a junior hospital doctor in America
E for east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An American medic is handed a coin and is held for the length of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a 25-cent coin but is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Internees are civilians confined in wartime for as long as hostilities last.

clue.text: What will help one in getting into Oxford?

definitions.text: What will help one in getting into Oxford?

parts.words: What will help one in getting into Oxford?
parts.note: an Oxford is a style of laced shoe, so the help is a tool for slipping a foot in

explanation.surface: Seeking advice on how to win admission to the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved tool eases the heel into footwear, and Oxfords are lace-up shoes.

clue.text: I started to say why leave Guyana for the Lizard!

indicators.note: leave means the letter named is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: the South American country is used as written
why is pronounced like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Someone begins explaining their departure from Guyana for the Lizard peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'why' stands for Y because they sound the same; remove Y from GUYANA and put I in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tropical American reptile is a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Pitch for Jack?

definitions.meaning: Jack ... is slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: Asking what to throw in place of a Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, like tar, is an old slang name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black resin like that used on roads, and a sailor is called a jack-tar.

clue.text: Submarine run eased off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A U-boat's voyage was cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals rearranging RUN and EASED; 'Submarine' is the adjective, beneath the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means located beneath the surface of the ocean.

clue.text: Saloon guys in opera

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car with an enclosed body
guys are men

explanation.surface: Fellows in a bar at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon is a British term for a four-door sedan car.
explanation.definitionFit: Bizet's best-known stage work is named after its gypsy heroine.

clue.text: Bond, say, given percentage upfront? He is taking risks, of course!

definitions.text: He is taking risks, of course!

indicators.note: upfront places the percentage word ahead of the spy word

parts.note: a commission is a percentage paid on a deal
James Bond is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A fictional spy, given a cut first, takes on danger.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is an old name for a bookmaker, who takes bets on horses running on a race course.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker accepts wagers on racecourse events, as a bettor's go-between.

clue.text: Bird down-under no longer?

parts.note: a flightless bird of New Zealand that has since died out

explanation.surface: Asking if an Australasian bird has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant flightless New Zealand bird was hunted to extinction centuries ago.

clue.text: Imitation tailless bear is cleaner

parts.note: a sham is a fake or imitation

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the bear's name is lopped off

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: A fake toy bear with no tail is something clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Winnie-the-Pooh is the bear; drop his final H.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid soap for washing hair or carpets.

clue.text: Not much of a break for Henry, the high flier

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an airline flies high

explanation.surface: A short holiday for Henry, the success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is a fracture, not a holiday: the answer is a very thin crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline fracture is the slightest crack in a bone.

clue.text: contraptions of daring young men?

parts.note: an allusion to those magnificent men in their flying contraptions and the daring young man on the flying trapeze

explanation.surface: Gadgets belonging to bold youths.
explanation.definitionFit: Contraptions are devices or apparatus, the flying ones of the famous film and song.

clue.text: Number of unpayed men inside, you might say

definitions.text: Number of unpayed men inside, you might say

parts.words: Number of unpayed men inside, you might say
parts.note: read 'inside' as 'in side': the count of amateur players in a rugby union team

explanation.surface: Counting unpaid prisoners.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union was long strictly amateur, and its team, or side, is of a set size.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union team has that many players.

clue.text: Swallow caught in the attic

indicators.note: caught in means the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A bird trapped up in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' looks like the bird but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to consume it.

clue.text: Venus of the light body?

definitions.meaning: the morning planet seen at dawn
the sun, the heavenly body giving daylight

explanation.surface: Asking whether the goddess is a luminous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the morning planet and the sun have been poetically called the star of day.

clue.text: M our acting vicar around Chichester?

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A vicar performing in the Sussex cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals rearranging M and OUR ACTING VICAR; Chichester is not the city but Sir Francis Chichester, who sailed solo round the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Chichester sailed single-handed around the globe in 1966-67.

clue.text: Maintain a lock can be turned

indicators.note: turned means the word for a lock of hair is read backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Claiming a lock is able to rotate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' is hair, not a door fastening: reversing TRESS gives SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to state it firmly.

clue.text: No returns on this ticket!

parts.note: a fare for a single outward journey, without the trip back

explanation.surface: A sign at a box office refusing refunds.
explanation.definitionFit: A single ticket covers travel in only one direction.

clue.text: Fellow dissembling, is taking to the air

parts.note: dissembling is lying

explanation.surface: A deceitful man is taking off.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking to the air means going aloft, in flight.

clue.text: Left senior nurse at home inside

indicators.note: inside places the home word within the nurse word

parts.note: in Britain a sister is a senior nurse
in means at home

explanation.surface: A ward sister went home and stayed indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is not departed but the heraldic left-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for left, and in heraldry the left-hand side.

clue.text: Take-home lacework?

explanation.surface: Lace taken home.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay is what remains after tax, and mesh fabric is netting.

clue.text: Sound of air force passing under bridge!

definitions.text: Sound of air force passing under bridge!

parts.words: Sound of air force passing under bridge!
parts.note: the bridge is that of the nose, and the air is forced out in a noisy blast

explanation.surface: Jet noise as a squadron flies beneath a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive expulsion of air through the nostrils, below the nose's bridge.

clue.text: Ordinary seaman first to be strange

indicators.note: first places the sailor before the ordinary word

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
ordinary means normal

explanation.surface: An ordinary seaman as the first oddity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary seaman' reads as one naval rank, but the two words do separate jobs; 'first' puts the sailor ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Abnormal means departing from the usual, so odd.
